hypotheses.title: Kinematic reactivation favourability gate (slip/dilation tendency × geodetic strain)
layers: USGS ScienceBase 6296974dd34ec53d276bb33d (DOI 10.5066/P9YL58W6) Shapefile_Full Study.zip (34.25 MB; slip & dilation tendency for Great Basin Quaternary faults)
hypotheses.signature: Per off-catalogue dot: local ridge strike vs INGENIOUS slip-tendency (Ts) and dilation-tendency (Td) fields interpolated from similarly oriented catalogued segments, multiplied by the local geodetic strain-second-invariant quantile. Prune unfavourable-oriented low-strain dots; protect favourable ones.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: The Siler (2022) product exists because favourably oriented faults 'may be likely to host as-yet-undiscovered hydrothermal processes' (DataCite abstract, verbatim). The Qfaults compilation is geomorphically biased; favourably oriented faults in active E-W extension keep accumulating geodetic strain and are the class expert mappers add even without crisp scarps.
hypotheses.confounders: The Ts/Td fields cover catalogued traces only; transfer to un-catalogued orientations assumes local stress homogeneity. Strike estimation from 100 m ridges has orientation noise; use sector smoothing.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H28-4/SRCOH used shear-rate x seismicity density (refuted 0/4 folds); no arm has used stress-orientation kinematics or the Siler product; this is an emission gate, not a GBDT feature injection (H31-1's failed mode).
